chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū ʿAmr al-Madāʾinī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: My father عليه السلام used to say: Indeed, Allah has decreed a decisive decree that He does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and then take it away from him until the servant commits a sin by which he deserves that punishment.

key_terms.النَّقِمَةَ: vengeance, punishment, or retribution deserved as a consequence
key_terms.بِنِعْمَةٍ: with a blessing or bounty granted by Allah
key_terms.ذَنْبًا: a sin committed by the servant
key_terms.فَيَسْلُبَهَا: then take it away or strip it away

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah remove blessings from a person according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the removal of divine blessings is tied to a servant’s sins and does not occur arbitrarily. It emphasizes divine justice and warns that wrongdoing can cause a person to become deserving of punishment and the loss of favor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Husayn Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Abu Amro Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Judged an absolute Judgement that He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Favour upon a servant with a Bounty then He<sup>azwj</sup> would Confiscate it from him unless the servant commits a new sin becoming deserving of that Vengeance’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Abu Ali al-Ash’ari have narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from abu ‘Amr al-Mada’ini who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘My father has said, “Allah has made a firm decision not to take away the blessing that He has granted to a servant of His until he commits a sin that subjects him to misfortune.’”
